clue.text: Carrier only used for old musical instrument

parts.note: a sack is a bag used to carry things
but can mean only, as in 'but a child'

explanation.surface: A bag-carrier was the only thing used to hold some antique instrument.
explanation.definitionFit: The sackbut is the Renaissance ancestor of the trombone, an early brass instrument.

clue.text: Jack's right

parts.note: jack tar is a sailor, so this is the sailor's word for the right-hand side of a ship

explanation.definitionFit: Sailors call the right-hand side of a vessel, facing forward, by this nautical term.

clue.text: Fabulous monster caught poor Hermia

parts.note: C is the cricket abbreviation for caught

indicators.note: poor suggests the letters of Hermia are in a bad state, reordered

explanation.surface: A mythical beast has captured unlucky Hermia.
explanation.walkthrough: Hermia is a character from A Midsummer Night's Dream.
explanation.definitionFit: The chimera of Greek myth was a fire-breathing beast with lion, goat and serpent parts.

clue.text: Unlimited but tied to a smaller number

parts.note: bound means tied up
less is a smaller amount

explanation.surface: Unrestricted, yet constrained to fewer people.
explanation.definitionFit: Something without bounds is infinite, having no limits.

clue.text: Drink taken by singer ?

definitions.meaning: split as ..., a high note that a soprano may take

explanation.surface: A drink is downed by a vocalist.
explanation.definitionFit: To drink habitually, and a top E, a high note sung.

clue.text: Refuse to supply dress before time

indicators.note: the dress word comes in front of the time word

parts.note: garb is clothing, dress
an age is a period of time

explanation.surface: Someone declines to provide a frock ahead of schedule.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Refuse' reads as a verb but is the noun, rubbish.
explanation.definitionFit: Refuse as a noun is rubbish, waste thrown away.

clue.text: Revolver turned to use by sword-maker ?

definitions.text: Revolver turned to use by sword-maker ?

parts.words: Revolver turned to use by sword-maker ?
parts.note: not a pistol but a rotating stone wheel that a swordsmith spins to sharpen blades

explanation.definitionFit: A revolving stone wheel on which blades are sharpened.

clue.text: Kingdom's old Spanish coin with monarch's head

parts.note: the real was a former Spanish silver coin

indicators.note: the head of a word is its first letter

explanation.surface: A kingdom's antique coin bearing the king's head.
explanation.definitionFit: A realm is a kingdom, the domain of a monarch.

clue.text: French theologian led Arab revolt

indicators.note: a revolt overturns the order of things, so these letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A French churchman headed an Arab uprising.
explanation.definitionFit: Peter Abelard was a twelfth-century French philosopher and theologian, lover of Heloise.

clue.text: Weird quarter on lake

parts.note: E, east, is one of the four quarters of the compass
Erie is one of the Great Lakes

explanation.surface: A strange district on the lakeside.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'on' means placed above.
explanation.definitionFit: Eerie and uncanny both describe something strange and unsettling.

clue.text: Last word in Paris fashion

parts.note: the French way of saying a final goodbye, not the newest style from Paris couture

explanation.definitionFit: The French farewell is literally the final word said when parting, in the Parisian manner.

clue.text: Soldier about to return by ship

parts.note: a private is the lowest rank of soldier

indicators.note: the little word for about is read backwards, coming home

parts.note: re means about, concerning

explanation.surface: A serviceman is about to go back home by sea.
explanation.definitionFit: A privateer was an armed private ship licensed to attack enemy shipping.

clue.text: Girl gets tip in bar, perhaps

indicators.note: the word for tip goes inside the rearranged letters
perhaps suggests a variant arrangement of the letters of bar

parts.note: an end is a tip, as of a finger

explanation.surface: A young woman receives a gratuity while working in a pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'perhaps' turns BAR into BRA, and 'in' puts END inside it.
explanation.definitionFit: Brenda is a girl's name.

clue.text: Drink from Eden river?

parts.note: the plain water that the first man in the Garden of Eden would have drunk from its river

explanation.definitionFit: A jocular old name for water, the only drink the first man had in Eden.

clue.text: TV programme gives people a cricket extra

parts.note: a nation is a people
a wide is a ball bowled out of reach, which gives the batting side an extra run

explanation.surface: A television show offers viewers a bonus run in cricket.
explanation.walkthrough: Nationwide was a BBC early-evening current-affairs programme of the 1970s.
explanation.definitionFit: Nationwide was a popular BBC magazine show broadcast in the evenings.

clue.text: A stern view of Omar's bidding

parts.note: the wake is the trail of water seen behind a boat's stern

explanation.surface: A look at the back of a ship, as Omar asked.
explanation.walkthrough: The Rubaiyat of Omar Khayyam, in FitzGerald's translation, opens with the command 'Awake!'.
explanation.definitionFit: The famous first word of FitzGerald's Rubaiyat is a command to rouse from sleep.

clue.text: Positions of some strikers ?

parts.note: strikers could be industrial protesters adopting stances of opinion, or batsmen and boxers taking up physical stances

explanation.definitionFit: Attitudes are both postures of the body and stances of opinion, as taken by strikers of either kind.

clue.text: Ancient conqueror in dull Arlen novel

parts.note: tame means dull, uninteresting

indicators.note: novel means new, so the letters of Arlen take a new order

explanation.surface: An old conqueror appears in a boring book by Arlen.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book by the writer Michael Arlen but signals rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Tamerlane, or Timur, was a fourteenth-century Turco-Mongol conqueror.

clue.text: Declaration might show possibility of drawing

definitions.meaning: a bank's account summary shows how much money can be withdrawn

explanation.definitionFit: A formal assertion, and a bank's account summary showing funds that can be drawn out.

clue.text: Summary no-one returned — it's needed after board meeting

parts.note: a digest is a summary of material

indicators.note: the letters for no and one are read backwards, going back

parts.note: NO plus I, the Roman numeral for one

explanation.surface: A precis came back unread by anyone, needed after the directors met.
explanation.walkthrough: 'board' is the dining table, not a company board: after a meal you need to digest it.
explanation.definitionFit: After a meal at the table, the body must break down the food it has eaten.

clue.text: Coward and criminal upset vessel

indicators.note: in a down clue upset turns the words upside down, reading them backwards

parts.note: Noel Coward, the English playwright
a lag is a convict

explanation.surface: A timid person and a crook overturned a boat.
explanation.walkthrough: 'upset' reverses NOEL LAG to give GAL LEON.
explanation.definitionFit: A galleon was a large sailing ship of the sixteenth and seventeenth centuries.

clue.text: In different degrees, many a poisonous snake

parts.note: MA, Master of Arts, is one degree
M, the Roman numeral for a thousand, stands for many
BA, Bachelor of Arts, is a different degree

explanation.surface: A deadly snake is found in many places to a varying extent.
explanation.walkthrough: 'In' is a link; the two degrees surround M.
explanation.definitionFit: The mamba is a highly venomous African snake.

clue.text: Might be guided by girl the priest brought up

parts.note: a miss is a girl

indicators.note: in a down clue brought up means read from bottom to top

parts.note: Eli was the priest who raised Samuel in the Bible

explanation.surface: Someone may be steered by a young woman the clergyman raised.
explanation.walkthrough: 'brought up' looks like upbringing but reverses ELI.
explanation.definitionFit: A guided missile is a weapon steered to its target, so this projectile might be guided.

clue.text: Evil-doers get in among the houses

indicators.note: the little word in goes among the letters of the houses

parts.note: villas are large houses

explanation.surface: Criminals break into a row of houses.
explanation.definitionFit: Villains are wicked people, criminals.

clue.text: Clothes or underclothes

definitions.meaning: a verb: dresses or robes someone, as in vesting a priest
a noun: undershirts worn beneath a shirt

explanation.definitionFit: To vest is to dress in robes, and undershirts are worn under other garments.

clue.text: Consent to some meagre emoluments

indicators.note: some says the answer is a run of letters hidden inside the words that follow

parts.note: the letters run across the end of one word into the next

explanation.surface: Someone accepts a pitiful salary.
explanation.definitionFit: To consent is to accept, say yes.

clue.text: Fish swears to reform

indicators.note: to reform is to remake, so the letters of swears are put into a new order

explanation.surface: A fish curses and vows to change its ways.
explanation.definitionFit: The wrasse is a brightly coloured sea fish.

clue.text: Making a move, I take it

definitions.text: Making a move, I take it

parts.words: Making a move, I take it
parts.note: the speaker is something you take when making a move on foot, a single pace

explanation.definitionFit: A pace is what you take when you move, taking a single stride.

clue.text: Plant southern fruit — a money-maker

parts.note: a pear is a fruit
the mint is where coins are made

explanation.surface: A grower puts in southern fruit trees hoping to make a fortune.
explanation.definitionFit: Spearmint is a common garden herb of the mint family.

clue.text: Quick return of bad article

indicators.note: the words for bad and the article are read backwards together

parts.note: evil means bad
a is the indefinite article

explanation.surface: A faulty item is swiftly sent back.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Quick' is the old sense, as in 'the quick and the dead'.
explanation.definitionFit: Quick in the archaic sense means living, as in the quick and the dead.

clue.text: Frank gets increase without a lot of trouble

indicators.note: the letters are put through a lot of trouble, mixed into a new order
without says a letter is left out of the word increase

explanation.surface: Frank gets a pay rise with very little difficulty.
explanation.walkthrough: Taking A from INCREASE leaves INCRESE, which is then rearranged.
explanation.definitionFit: Frank and honest both describe someone open and genuine.

clue.text: Tense before changing for nets

parts.note: pre is a prefix meaning before

indicators.note: changing tells us to alter the order of the letters of nets

explanation.surface: Nervous before swapping the goal nets.
explanation.definitionFit: The present is a grammatical tense, alongside past and future.
